subject: [Fix] Don't write conv state from the fused KDA verify kernel (#39524)
pr_body:
> Reland of #39219, which was reverted in #39405 because it was merged by mistake.

## Motivation

`fused_kda_conv_gating_verify` rolled the conv state back into `conv_state` at the end of the kernel. Every V tile loads that same Q/K conv history at entry, but only `i_v == 0` writes it, so a tile scheduled in a later wave reads what the owner already overwrote.

The writeback is also dead: verify is speculative, and the commit scatter sets `conv_state` from the selected intermediate window. `accept_lens` is at least 1, so `last_correct_step_indices` is never negative for a real request and the scatter always overwrites.

So the stores are removed rather than guarded. `conv_state` and the SSM state are read-only in verify.

## Modifications

| | |
| --- | --- |
| kernel | drop the 9 `tl.store(cs_base, ...)` at the end of `fused_kda_conv_gating_verify_kernel` |
| docstring | state ownership: conv and SSM state are read-only, the commit scatter advances them |
| tests | `conv_state` must come back untouched; output must not vary with CTA scheduling |

Reached only with `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_KDA_VERIFY=1` (default off), on the KDA Triton verify path at `topk == 1`.

## How the race shows

H=1 with HV=16, so 16 V tiles share one Q/K history. Same inputs, against the unfused pair:

| | max abs | max rel |
| --- | --- | --- |
| full GB300, one wave | 2.98e-8 | 7.2e-3 |
| 8-SM green context, waves serialized | **5.0e-2** | **188** |

Removing the stores makes both configurations identical. The residual ~1 ulp is reduction-order difference and is unaffected by the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

Ling-3.0-flash BF16, 4x GB300 TP4, NEXTN, fused verify on. Full GSM8K, thinking on, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=8192`, 1 repeat.

| | score | stop | error |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before | 96.06% | 99.70% | 0.00% |
| after | 95.83% | 99.17% | 0.00% |

Unchanged — the gap is inside the ~0.55pp 1-sigma band at n=1319. The race is below eval resolution when the grid fits one wave.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same server, 8192 in / 1024 out at concurrency 1, 64 warmup, `--flush-cache`, 3 runs per arm. Accept length 3.01 on all …[truncated]

subject: [Bugfix] Fix mHC block-M prenorm GEMM cross-row reduction carry-over (#49429)
pr_body:
In hc_prenorm_gemm_block_m_tilelang, T.alloc_var(init=0.0) declared inside the unrolled i_m loop is hoisted and initialized only once, so the cross-warp reduction accumulator carries over between the rows of a block: every odd output row (and its sqrsum) is the sum of both rows in its block. The block-M kernel is selected for num_tokens >= 1024, so DeepSeek-V4 mHC prefill produces corrupted mixes for odd tokens whenever the DeepGEMM path is not in use. Use per-row locals instead.

Verified on B200: odd-row output equaled ref(even)+ref(odd) exactly and odd-row sqrsum was 2x before the fix; all
tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py cases pass after (including the previously failing num_tokens=2048 parametrizations).

subject: [DeepSeek-V4] Fix idle-rank dummy-extend sparse-prefill crash under DP breakable CUDA graph (#31705)
pr_body:
## Problem

`test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_b200.py` (base-c b200 deepep, BCG recipe: TP4/DP4/DeepEP, `--enable-mixed-chunk --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`) crashes deterministically on idle DP ranks:

```
_forward_prefill_sparse: assert core_attn_metadata.c4_sparse_raw_indices is not None
AssertionError: sparse-prefill c4 path requires c4_sparse_raw_indices
```

## Root cause

Latent defect from #30898, surfaced by #31487.

Under DP attention + breakable prefill CUDA graph (#30898), an idle rank is padded into a fabricated dummy EXTEND: `forward_batch_info` stashes the real mode in `_original_forward_mode` (IDLE) and sets `forward_mode = EXTEND`. `_get_logical_forward_mode` returns the stale IDLE, so metadata is built via the decode branch (no `c4_sparse_raw_indices`, gated on `is_prefill=True`), while the forward keys off `forward_mode = EXTEND` and runs `_forward_prefill_sparse` (default-on since #29775) → assertion.

Latent since 7-12; #31487 ("avoid excessive prefill CUDA graph padding") then made DP prefill land on the small capture buckets (4/16) where the dummy extend actually fires, flipping the job green→red (bisected: last green `0ad0ff2e9e`, first red `216b750c`).

## Fix

Build metadata for the mode the forward actually runs: when `forward_mode == EXTEND`, return it instead of the stale `_original_forward_mode`, so extend metadata is built and `c4_sparse_raw_indices` is allocated. The fabricated batch already carries valid extend fields. `TARGET_VERIFY` overwrites (MTP hybrid SSM) still prefer `_original_forward_mode`.

## Validation

Reproduced + fixed on a 4×B200 devbox at `216b750c` (exact BCG args, shipped code): before, crashes under load (idle ranks DP1/2/3); after, 204/204 requests OK, 0 assertions. Crash/liveness verified under synthetic load; gsm8k accuracy left to CI.

---

subject: [Bugfix] Allocate packed outputs in fused_q_kv_rmsnorm so q_b_proj keeps its low-latency GEMM path at decode (#53109)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a silent performance bug: `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm` allocates its outputs with `torch.empty_like(qr)`, but `qr`/`kv` are column slices of the fused `qkv_a` projection output. PyTorch preserves the strides of size-1 dims, so at `num_tokens == 1` (single-sequence decode) `empty_like` returns a tensor carrying the **parent buffer's row stride** — e.g. `(2112, 1)` for a `[1, 1536]` `q_c` slice:

```python
>>> qkv = torch.empty(1, 2112)
>>> q = qkv[:, :1536]
>>> torch.empty_like(q).stride()
(2112, 1)   # is_contiguous() is True, but not packed row-major
```

The Kimi-K3 low-latency GEMM dispatch (`low_latency_gemm._is_packed_row_major`, which requires `stride == (shape[1], 1)`) then rejects `q_c`, and `q_b_proj` silently falls back to `F.linear` → cuBLAS on **every decode step**, even though `(2304, 1536)` is listed in `KIMI_K3_PROJECTIONS`. `num_tokens >= 2` happens to produce packed strides, so only decode is affected — which is why this never showed up in prefill or batched benchmarks.

The fallback is not just a missed fusion. On one SM103 machine (148 SMs) the cuBLAS heuristic picks `nvjet_sm103_tst_16x64_64x16_2x1_v_bz_TNN` at ~10.9 µs/call for this `[1,1536]×[1536,2304]` GEMM, vs 4.5 µs (in-graph) for the intended `dsv3_fused_a` kernel — ~150 µs per decode step across Kimi-K3's 24 MLA layers at TP8. On another SM103 machine (152 SMs) the heuristic happens to land on a faster kernel (~3.1 µs), so the cost of this bug is machine-dependent and easy to miss.

Fix: allocate packed row-major outputs explicitly. Packed outputs are strictly better for every downstream consumer of these tensors.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm.py
```

Adds `test_fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_outputs_are_packed`, which feeds column slices of a fused buffer (the real call pattern from `mla.py`) at `num_tokens ∈ {1, 16}` and asserts packed output strides plus numerical correctness. The `num_tokens == 1` case fails before this change (`stride (768, 1) != (192, 1)`) and passes after.

End-to-end A/B on Kimi-K3, TP8, single 8×GPU SM103 node (`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, isl 128 / osl 32, torch-profiled serving, identical config exc …[truncated]

subject: [Bugfix] Fix accuracy issue for silu_mul + nvfp4 quant fusion kernel (#24833)

- Fix accuracy issue for silu_mul + nvfp4 quant fusion kernel
  - In previous #23671, the original author used an approximate way to compute silu. The sigmoid was computed by `tanh(x/2) * 0.5 + 0.5`, while the standard definition should be `1 / (1 + e^(-x))`.

subject: [Bugfix][ROCm][performance] Resolve the performance regression issue of the Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking under rocm_atten (#32336)
pr_body: ## Purpose This PR resolves a significant performance regression for models using non-standard block sizes (specifically block size 544, such as Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking) under the ROCM_ATTN backend. Background: Recently, PR #31712 restricted the supported kernel block sizes for ROCM_ATTN to only 16 and 32. While this was intended to prevent unsupported configurations, it inadvertently throttled models that rely on larger, non-standard block sizes (previously optimized in PR #31380). This led to a massive degradation in TTFT and overall throughput for these models. This PR ensures that ROCM_ATTN correctly recognizes and supports these specialized block sizes again, restoring the optimized performance path for Qwen3-Next and similar architectures. ## Test Plan We conducted comprehensive benchmarks on AMD GPUs with tensor_parallel_size=2 to verify the fix and ensure no regressions for standard models. subject: [AMD] fix(jit): port kv_canary write/verify/plan kernels to ROCm (#28357)
pr_body:
## Summary

Make the **kv_canary JIT kernels** (`write`, `verify`, `plan_entries`) compile and run correctly under hipcc/ROCm, and onboard their JIT unit tests to the `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` suite. All ROCm-specific behavior is gated behind `USE_ROCM` so the **CUDA/NV path is unchanged**. This unblocks the kv_canary e2e tests on AMD (stacked follow-up).

Builds on the activation ROCm fix from #27947 (already merged to `main`), which is what lets `jit-kernel-unit-test-amd` compile end-to-end.

## Changes

**Kernel port (`python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/kv_canary/*.cuh`):**

1. **Device matching** — replace hardcoded `kDLCUDA` with the platform-agnostic `kDLGPU` alias in all `TensorMatcher` `set_options`/`with_device` calls. The previous `kDLCUDA` constraint raises a runtime `Device mismatch` on ROCm, where torch tensors export as `kDLROCM`. `kDLGPU` is `kDLCUDA` on CUDA and `kDLROCM` on ROCm (defined in `sgl_kernel/utils.cuh`), so this is a **compile-time no-op on NV**. CPU-side params (`kDLCPU`) are unchanged.

2. **Verify-kernel `slot_run_counter` reduction (ROCm-only)** — the hand-rolled `__shfl_down_sync(0xFFFFFFFFu, …)` loop assumes a 32-lane warp and crosses the 32-lane boundary on AMD wave64, miscounting. Gated behind `#ifndef USE_ROCM`/`#else`:
   - **CUDA**: keeps the original `__shfl_down_sync` down-reduction and `threadIdx.x & 31u` leader, byte-for-byte (codegen unchanged).
   - **ROCm**: uses the warp-size-agnostic `device::warp::reduce_sum<kWarpThreads>` (width-32 xor all-reduce), keeping the reduction within 32-lane sub-groups on wave64. The `warp.cuh` include is likewise `#ifdef USE_ROCM`.

3. **Plan-kernel ROCm build fixes (ROCm-only, NV untouched):**
   - Guard the CUDA-only `#include <cuda_runtime.h>` behind `#ifndef USE_ROCM` (hipcc has no such header; the write/verify kernels compile without it).
   - Replace the CUDA-only `__trap()` device builtin with `__builtin_trap()` on ROCm (clang builtin; `__trap()` is undeclared under hipcc). Same contract-break device abort.

**Test onboarding:**

subject: [Bugfix] Support -1 (invalid/non-local) slots in topk_ids for Triton MoE (#46408)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Under expert parallelism, dispatch hands the experts a `topk_ids` tensor whose entries can be `-1`, marking invalid / non-local slots (a token's routed expert lives on another rank). The Triton unfused MoE path (`gpt_oss_triton_kernels_moe.py`) mishandled these in two places:

1. **`expert_map[topk_ids]`** (global→local remap) indexed the map with `-1`, which wraps to `expert_map[-1]` — a valid local id — and misroutes the slot. Replaced with a fused `remap_topk_to_local` kernel that preserves `-1` (the skip sentinel `make_routing_data` expects).
2. **`ops.moe_sum`** reduced over all `topk` slots, but `matmul_ogs` leaves the `-1` (non-local) slots **unwritten** in the intermediate buffer, so the sum folded in uninitialized garbage (and was NaN-unsafe). Replaced with a `masked_moe_sum` kernel that skips `-1` slots in the per-token reduction.

Both replace prior multi-op sequences with a single fused kernel. The now-unused `from vllm import _custom_ops as ops` import and the `moe_sum` wrapper are removed.

For the non-EP case (`expert_map is None`, no `-1`), behavior is unchanged: `remap_topk_to_local` is not called, and `masked_moe_sum` over all-valid slots equals the previous `moe_sum`.

### Naming note
`remap_topk_to_local` is deliberately **not** named `apply_expert_map`: a scalar `@triton.jit` device helper `apply_expert_map(expert_id, expert_map)` already exists in `deep_gemm_utils.py` (tested by #46061). This kernel is a different thing — a launchable, vectorized remap over a whole `topk_ids` tensor — so it gets a distinct name.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs for `masked_moe_sum`, `apply_expert_map`, `expert_map topk_ids`. #46061 only adds a unit test for the existing DeepGemm device helper; #42034 fixes a padding sentinel in the FlashInfer one-sided path (different backend). Neither addresses `-1` handling in the Triton unfused path.

## Test plan

- Lint/type: `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy` (via pre-commit) pass on the touched file.
- Functional: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GB200 ×4, `dp=4 -ep`, Triton MoE backend with EP dispatch producing `-1` slots — GSM8K ~95%. Without this fix the path produces garbage output (mis-mapped `-1` and garb …[truncated]

subject: [ROCm] Fix QuickReduce fp16 saturation corrupting bf16 all-reduces (106M non-finite -> 0, +0.3%) (#34484)
pr_body:
Fixes #34473.

## Summary

QuickReduce converts BF16 inputs to FP16 before reduction for performance. GPT-OSS reaches magnitudes above FP16's maximum finite value (65,504), so the conversion could produce `inf`; quantized codecs then propagated that value through a 32-element block.

This PR:

- Enables `MODE.FP16_OVFL` on both gfx942 and gfx950 so FP16 overflow clamps instead of becoming non-finite.
- Uses a power-of-two range guard (`S = 16`) for `CodecFP`, scaling in FP32 before narrowing and restoring the scale on output.
- Emits `v_cvt_pk_f16_f32` explicitly for the scaled `CodecFP` conversion. This prevents LLVM from moving the FP16 conversion ahead of the scale.
- Keeps `CodecQ4/Q6/Q8` at `S = 1` on the existing fast FP16 path. Their block scaling already normalizes values, and a larger cast scale moves the reciprocal-scale saturation cliff into real data.
- Adds a four-GPU regression test covering low values, ordinary values, sums above FP16 range, individual inputs above FP16 range, negative overflow, and mixed blocks.

## Scope

This fixes the GPT-OSS non-finite-output failure without routing quantized codecs through native BF16 kernels. Quantized reductions may still clamp finite values when their FP16 accumulator exceeds 65,504; that is pre-existing lossy behavior and is intentionally left unchanged here. The native-BF16 alternative was numerically exact but 22–46% slower.

## Validation

- Built and passed the TP4 range regression on MI350X and MI355X with ROCm 7.2.
- `CodecFP` is bit-exact for all tested cases, including inputs and sums above FP16 range.
- Quantized codecs remain bit-exact for low and ordinary values and produce finite outputs for overflow cases.
- Captured GPT-OSS reductions went from non-finite outputs to zero non-finite outputs.
- PR-base versus final-patch latency on MI350X showed no measurable regression:
  - INT8/INT6/INT4: within 0.4% at 16 MiB and within 0.1% at 90 MiB.
  - FP: 9.6% faster at 16 MiB and 1.1% faster at 90 MiB in this run.
- Repository pre-commit checks pass.

## Test plan

pr_body:
Companion AITER fix: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4530 (making this PR fix redundant once the AITER fix is merged, released, and AITER pin in vLLM is updated).

## Purpose

This PR hot-fixes

tests/models/quantization/test_gpt_oss.py::test_gpt_oss_attention_quantization[amd/gpt-oss-20b-MoE-Quant-W-MXFP4-A-FP8-KV-FP8-0.89-1]
```

that started failing in ROCm vLLM following AITER version bump from `0.1.16.post5` to `0.1.19` (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49361) as seen in [mi355_1: Quantized Models Test](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11528/list?sid=019fb767-0fce-4570-b9af-a4ba0421b3d5&tab=output), with:

Memory access fault by GPU node-2 (Agent handle: 0x3a0749c0) on address 0x7de557bcb000. Reason: Unknown.
^[_bk;t=1785489648144 GPU coredump: execvp failed: No such file or directory
^[_bk;t=1785489648216 Failed to write program header to pipe: Broken pipe
^[_bk;t=1785489648216 GPU coredump: handler exited with error (status: 1)
^[_bk;t=1785489648216 GPU core dump failed

To make it short: a seemingly harmless change in https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4198 resulted in AITER's triton MOE routing to start to wrongfully handle token rows containing `inf`/`-inf`/`nan`, which is the case with HIP Graph in vLLM (e.g. `tokens_unpadded=7`, `tokens_padded=8` to dispatch on a recorded graph, and the last row containing dummy meaningless data).

subject: [CI] Fix race condition with StatelessProcessGroup.barrier (#18506)
pr_body:
First, this includes one small security fix to the test_shm_broadcast
test.  Don't use the host's default IP address for this test. Use
localhost.  Otherwise we are binding a socket to an IP address that is
externally reachable. If the host does not have a proper firewall
configuration and is exposed to potentially untrusted traffic, this
would open a short window of time where the host is vulnerable to remote
code execution via pickle deserialization while the test is running.

The real fix included here is to resolve a race condition with the
`barrier()` implementation in `StatelessProcessGroup`. The barrier was
used to synchronize processes in this test, but it did not properly
ensure that the underlying `TCPStore` instance in the
`StatelessProcessGroup` would not be destroyed before other processes in
the group were finished using it. The fix here is a more robust
`barrier()` implementation that does 3 key things:

1. Signal arrival into the barrier.

2. Make all processes wait to receive the signal from all other
   processes that they have arrived in the barrier.

3. For rank 0 only, the one that runs the server side of the `TCPStore`
   instance, ensure it is that last process to exit the barrier by
   waiting until it receives a signal from all other processes that they
   have departed.

Prior to this change, the test failure in issue #18492 was very easy for
me to reproduce - reliably in under 10 tries. With this change in place,
I have not seen the failure occur again (after a couple hundred runs so
far).

Closes #18492

Signed-off-by: Russell Bryant <rbryant@redhat.com>

subject: [diffusion] fix: run an all-valid attention mask on the backend's unmasked kernel (#41309)
pr_body:
## Problem

On sm100 the default attention backend resolves to `DYNAMIC_CUDNN_SDPA`, but `USPAttention`'s masked local path opens its varlen fast path only for `backend == FA`. Every other backend gets a dense additive mask for `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention`, and any mask moves SDPA off flash and cuDNN onto PyTorch's `fmha_cutlassF_*_sm80` kernel, even when the mask masks nothing.

Ideogram4 passes such a mask on both guidance branches at batch 1: its text is never padded at batch 1, so `segment_ids > 0` is all true. Every attention call on B200 therefore took the cutlassF path:

- torch profile of the denoising loop: attention = **54% of GPU time on 1×B200, 47% at TP2**, all in `fmha_cutlassF_bf16_aligned_32x128_gmem_sm80`
- per call (`[1, 18, 4126, 256]` bf16): **2.19 ms with the mask, 0.81 ms without**

It is also consistent with Ideogram4 measuring only ~9% faster on B200 than on H200, against 1.7-2.6× for the other models: on Hopper the default backend is FA, whose varlen path already treats an all-valid mask as dense.

## Fix

When `attn_mask_meta` shows every key valid (its index count equals the mask's element count, known on the host, no device sync), the masked local path runs the backend's own unmasked kernel. Segmented-prefix inputs (Qwen-Image) are concatenated first, so the prefix is kept. Masks with real padding, and meta without indices (padding-gap meta), keep the masked path. The FA backend is untouched (its varlen branch returns before this point), and so are the sequence-parallel paths.

## Validation (4×B200)

- Unit: the new `test/unit/test_usp_all_valid_key_mask.py` drives `USPAttention.forward` through the masked local branch with real varlen meta. An all-valid mask runs the backend kernel once and matches unmasked attention; a real padding mask, and padding-gap meta without indices, keep the masked path; a segmented prefix is concatenated before dispatch. The two backend-kernel tests fail on `main`. The neighbouring attention/mask unit tests (ring tail-pad, K/V gather, varlen meta, replicated prefix, Ideogram4, BCG padding) pass.

- Ideogram4 serving, default B200 command (`--tp-size 2`), warmup then 5 measured reques …[truncated]
